summary: The linear arboricity conjecture (la(G) = ⌈(k+1)/2⌉ for every k-regular graph G) remains open in full generality. The conjecture is confirmed for k ≤ 3 (cubic graphs, classical). Best known general upper bound as of 2025 is la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(log n) (Christoph et al., 2025), an exponential improvement over the O(Δ^{2/3}) error of Ferber–Fox–Jain (2018). The conjecture is also verified for 2k-regular graphs with girth ≥ 2k (Mishra, 2025).

since_posted.title: Towards the linear arboricity conjecture
since_posted.authors: Ferber, A., Fox, J., Jain, V.
since_posted.claim: Proves la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(Δ^{2/3−α}) for some α > 0 and gives probabilistic poly-time algorithms; improves the 1992 Alon–Spencer bound but does not settle the conjecture.

since_posted.title: New bounds for linear arboricity and related problems
since_posted.authors: Christoph, M., Draganıć, N., Girão, A., Hurley, E., Michel, L., Müyesser, A.
since_posted.claim: Proves every graph of maximum degree Δ decomposes into at most Δ/2 + O(log n) linear forests, an exponential improvement over prior error terms when Δ = Ω(n^ε); full conjecture (Δ/2 + O(1)) remains open.

since_posted.title: The Linear Arboricity Conjecture for Graphs with Large Girth
since_posted.claim: Proves the linear arboricity conjecture for 2k-regular graphs with girth g(G) ≥ 2k using a network-flow construction; also gives weaker bounds for smaller girth (la ≤ k+2 if g ≥ k, etc.).

notes: Conjecture confirmed for k=1,2,3 (classical; cubic case la=2 follows by DFS in linear time). The full conjecture for all k is open; the gap between proven bound Δ/2+O(log n) and conjectured bound ⌈(Δ+1)/2⌉ = Δ/2+O(1) is now logarithmic. Deciding whether la(G)=Δ/2 for even Δ is NP-complete (making exact determination hard in general). Corpus record arXiv:2302.13312 tracks a related refinement for planar graphs. Title and full author name for arXiv:2512.11240 were not returned by WebFetch; the URL and main result were confirmed.
